parsed.summary: The first theorem asserts that there exist two finitely generated, ICC, property-(T) countable groups Γ and Λ that are not isomorphic but have trace-preservingly *-isomorphic group von Neumann algebras. This is the two-group counterexample to Connes's conjecture. The second theorem is meant to formalize the infinite family of Theorem 1.2, but it quantifies universally (∀ Λ Γ) where the paper needs an existential. As written it claims every group and every sequence of groups has all these properties, which is false (take Λ trivial).

glossary.plain: A countable group bundled as a type with a group structure
G is infinite and every nonidentity conjugacy class is infinite
There is a group isomorphism G ≅ H
For every finite K ⊆ G and every ε > 0 there is a unit vector ξ with ‖π(g)ξ − ξ‖ < ε for all g ∈ K
Every unitary representation on a complex Hilbert space in universe u with almost invariant unit vectors has a nonzero invariant vector
glossary.note: Only Hilbert spaces in universe 0 are quantified over; this is adequate for countable groups.

glossary.plain: Bicommutant of {λ(g)} (together with adjoints) in B(ℓ²G)
The equivalence preserves projection suprema, where the order and suprema are defined algebraically inside the algebra
glossary.note: This condition is automatic for any *-algebra isomorphism. That is harmless, since *-isomorphisms of von Neumann algebras are automatically normal.

glossary.plain: There is a trace-preserving *-isomorphism L(G) ≅ L(H)
glossary.note: For II1 factors the trace condition is automatic. The Lean version is at least as strong as plain isomorphism.

lean_claims.plain: There exist countable groups Γ, Λ (in Type 0) that are finitely generated, ICC and have property (T), with L(Γ) ≅ L(Λ) trace-preservingly, and Γ ≇ Λ.

For EVERY countable group Λ and EVERY sequence (Γ_n) of countable groups, all of the following hold: all are f.g., ICC and have property (T); L(Γ_n) ≅ L(Λ); L(Γ_m) ≅ L(Γ_n); Γ_m ≇ Γ_n for m ≠ n; and Λ ≇ Γ_n.

paper_claims.plain: There exist finitely generated ICC property-(T) groups Λ, Γ_0, Γ_1, … that are pairwise nonisomorphic with L(Γ_n) ≅ L(Λ). Moreover, Γ_n contains a subgroup isomorphic to Γ_0 of index 2^{4n}, so the Γ_n are mutually commensurable.
The pair Λ, Γ_0 disproves Connes's rigidity conjecture.

coverage.why: Existence of two nonisomorphic f.g. ICC property-(T) groups with isomorphic group factors.
A universal quantifier replaces the existential, so the Lean statement is false rather than the paper's claim.
No commensurability or index statement appears in the Lean file.

flags.explanation: The statement begins with ∀ (Λ) (Γ : ℕ → …) instead of ∃. It therefore asserts that every group is f.g., ICC and has property (T), and so on. This is false: the trivial group is not infinite, hence not ICC. The statement does not capture Theorem 1.2 and is unprovable.
flags.probe_idea: Prove the negation: take Λ the trivial group (e.g. PUnit with a Countable instance) and derive ¬ IsICC Λ from ¬ Infinite PUnit.

flags.explanation: The 'moreover' part is omitted: Γ_n has a subgroup ≅ Γ_0 of index 2^{4n}, so the Γ_n are mutually commensurable.

The 'normality' condition uses suprema defined purely algebraically within the algebra. It is therefore preserved by any *-isomorphism and is vacuous rather than a genuine normality condition. This is harmless because *-isomorphisms of von Neumann algebras are automatically normal.
flags.probe_idea: Prove that every A ≃⋆ₐ[ℂ] B satisfies IsNormalStarAlgEquiv.

lint_verdicts.why: This is subtraction in a Hilbert space, not ℕ.
Rewriting the ℓ² norm with exponent 2; no junk value is involved.
Reindexing of a tsum by an equivalence; the exponent is 2.
